title: Hamlet
name: Hamlet
description: Hamlet (c. 1599-1601, William Shakespeare; England). Prince Hamlet of Denmark, home from university for his father's funeral, learns from his father's Ghost that King Claudius murdered him and married Queen Gertrude. Hamlet feigns madness, stages a play to catch Claudius's conscience, kills the eavesdropping Polonius, is sent to England, returns to find Ophelia mad and drowned, and dies in a rigged duel with Laertes - after which Fortinbras claims the throne. Themes: Revenge and delay; appearance vs. reality; mortality; madness real and feigned. The most famous play in world literature; its soliloquies defined modern consciousness of the self.

title: Macbeth
name: Macbeth
description: Macbeth (1606, William Shakespeare; England). Three witches hail the Scottish general Macbeth as future king. Spurred by Lady Macbeth, he murders King Duncan, seizes the throne, and descends into tyranny and paranoia - ordering Banquo's murder and the slaughter of Macduff's family. Lady Macbeth sleepwalks into madness and death; Macbeth is slain by Macduff, 'none of woman born,' and Malcolm restores order. Themes: Ambition; guilt; the supernatural; the unsexing of nature. Shakespeare's shortest tragedy and his most intense study of moral corruption.

title: King Lear
name: King Lear
description: King Lear (1605-1606, William Shakespeare; England). Aging King Lear divides his kingdom between flattering daughters Goneril and Regan, banishing honest Cordelia and loyal Kent. Betrayed and cast out into a storm, Lear descends into madness on the heath with his Fool, while Gloucester is blinded for loyalty. Cordelia returns with French forces but is hanged; Lear dies of grief bearing her body. Themes: Filial ingratitude; madness and insight; justice and suffering; nothingness. Often called the greatest of all plays; its storm scenes and final tableau are the summit of tragic art.

title: Othello
name: Othello
description: Othello (1603-1604, William Shakespeare; England). Othello, the Moorish general of Venice, secretly marries Desdemona. His ensign Iago, passed over for promotion, plants suspicion that Desdemona loves Cassio, manufacturing 'proof' from a lost handkerchief. Maddened by jealousy, Othello smothers Desdemona, learns the truth too late, and kills himself; Iago is led off to torture. Themes: Jealousy; race and otherness; manipulation; love destroyed by doubt. The most domestic of the great tragedies; Iago is literature's supreme villain.

title: Romeo and Juliet

description: Romeo and Juliet (c. 1595-1596, William Shakespeare; England). In feud-divided Verona, Romeo Montague loves Juliet Capulet at first sight; they marry secretly with Friar Laurence's help. After Romeo kills Juliet's cousin Tybalt, he is banished; Juliet fakes her death to escape marrying Paris, but Romeo, misinformed, poisons himself at her tomb. Waking to find him dead, Juliet stabs herself, and the families reconcile over their children's bodies. Themes: Young love vs. old hate; fate; haste; the feud. The archetypal love tragedy; its balcony scene is the most famous love scene ever written.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
name: A Midsummer Night's Dream
description: A Midsummer Night's Dream (c. 1595-1596, William Shakespeare; England). On the eve of Duke Theseus's wedding, four Athenian lovers flee to a forest where the fairy king Oberon and queen Titania quarrel over a changeling boy. Puck's love-juice misfires, scrambling all affections, while rude mechanicals rehearse a play for the wedding. By dawn all is sorted: three weddings, and Puck's epilogue asks the audience's pardon. Themes: Love's irrationality; dreams vs. waking; art and illusion; the green world. Shakespeare's most magical comedy; the rude mechanicals' play-within-a-play is pure theatrical joy.

title: The Tempest
name: The Tempest
description: The Tempest (1610-1611, William Shakespeare; England). Prospero, deposed Duke of Milan, has ruled an island for twelve years with his daughter Miranda, his spirit Ariel, and the monstrous Caliban. He raises a tempest to wreck his usurping brother Antonio and King Alonso, then orchestrates Miranda's love for Alonso's son Ferdinand, confronts his enemies, forgives them, frees Ariel, and drowns his magic book. Themes: Power and forgiveness; colonization; art vs. nature; the magician as artist. Shakespeare's farewell to the stage; Prospero's epilogue is the playwright's own goodbye.

title: Oedipus Rex

description: Oedipus Rex (c. 429 BC, Sophocles; Athens). King Oedipus of Thebes, famed for solving the Sphinx's riddle, vows to find King Laius's murderer and end a plague. title: Antigone
name: Antigone
description: Antigone (c. 441 BC, Sophocles; Athens). After the brothers Eteocles and Polynices kill each other, King Creon forbids burial of the traitor Polynices. Their sister Antigone defies the edict and buries him; Creon walls her in a tomb despite his son Haemon's pleas. Too late Creon relents: Antigone has hanged herself, Haemon kills himself, and Queen Eurydice follows - leaving Creon alone with his ruin. Themes: Divine law vs. human law; conscience vs. state; pride. The foundational tragedy of civil disobedience; Antigone's 'no' echoes through history.

title: A Doll's House
name: A Doll's House
description: A Doll's House (1879, Henrik Ibsen; Norway). Nora Helmer, the 'lark' of her banker husband Torvald, secretly borrowed money years ago to save his life, forging her father's signature. When the lender Krogstad threatens exposure, Torvald rages at her - then forgives her only when the danger passes. Seeing his love is conditional, Nora walks out, slamming the door on her doll's house marriage. Themes: Women's independence; marriage as performance; truth vs. comfortable lies. The door slam heard round the world; the founding play of modern drama.

title: Hedda Gabler

description: Hedda Gabler (1890, Henrik Ibsen; Norway). Hedda, daughter of a general, has married the dull scholar Tesman and is already bored to death. Facing blackmail and exposure, Hedda shoots herself. Themes: Power and boredom; beauty vs. respectability; the destructive will. Ibsen's most enigmatic heroine; a tragedy of a woman with no outlet for her force.

title: The Cherry Orchard

description: The Cherry Orchard (1904, Anton Chekhov; Russia). Lyubov Ranevskaya returns to her beloved estate, but debts force the sale of the cherry orchard. Old Firs is forgotten and left behind as the house is locked. Themes: Change and paralysis; memory; the end of an era; comedy in tragedy. Chekhov's last play; the sound of the breaking string haunts modern theater.

title: Uncle Vanya
name: Uncle Vanya
description: Uncle Vanya (1899, Anton Chekhov; Russia). On a decaying country estate, Vanya and his niece Sonya have worked for years to support the professor Serebryakov, who now arrives with his young wife Yelena and announces he will sell the estate. Themes: Wasted lives; work as salvation; resignation. Chekhov's great play of middle-aged despair and Sonya's transcendent final speech.

title: Three Sisters

description: Three Sisters (1901, Anton Chekhov; Russia). The Prozorov sisters - Olga, Masha, Irina - dream of returning to Moscow from their provincial garrison town. Jack Worthing (Ernest in town) and Algernon Moncrieff (Ernest in the country) both invent alter egos to escape duty; both love women - Gwendolen and Cecily - who insist on marrying someone named Ernest. title: Mother Courage and Her Children
name: Mother Courage and Her Children
description: Mother Courage and Her Children (1941, Bertolt Brecht; Germany/Switzerland). Anna Fierling, Mother Courage, follows the Thirty Years' War with her canteen wagon, profiting from the war that devours her children one by one: Eilif is executed, Swiss Cheese shot, and mute Kattrin is killed drumming to warn a town. Courage harnesses herself to the wagon again and trudges on. Themes: War as business; capitalism; the cost of survival. Brecht's greatest epic play; Kattrin's drum is theater's most shattering silence.
